{"answer": "It depends on the release. Per the spec (specs/support-agent-conversation-data/spec.md), the behaviour changed when the HAL Engine release `hal-engine-session-lifetime` (#117) landed. That release stops the engine from calling `delete` when a connection closes.

Before that release (FR-012, FR-066, from #23): `store.delete(sessionId)` is only cache eviction. It returns true but leaves the stored document, so `repository.load(sessionId)` still returns the conversation. Erasing a conversation then has to go through `eraseConversation(sessionId)` on the repository (FR-011).

From that release on (FR-013 to FR-017 and FR-065, from #152): `PersistentSessionStore.delete` is the GDPR erasure primitive. It erases the stored document first, then evicts the cache entry. It returns `Promise<boolean>`: true if a document or cache entry was removed, false if neither existed. After `await store.delete(id)` on a persisted conversation, both `repository.load(id)` and `store.get(id)` are `undefined`. If the repository's `eraseConversation` rejects, `delete` rejects and the session stays in the cache, so a partial erasure is never reported as done.

So the target behaviour is that it erases the stored conversation as well as the cache. I could not confirm from the sources which release of the engine is installed or whether #152 has shipped.", "sources": ["specs/support-agent-conversation-data/spec.md", "issue-152", "issue-591", "issue-587"]}
